facts.fact: The hounds of Kettamala number fourteen and sleep in a long kennel behind the stables; before the wedding they ran the yard loose from dusk to dawn.
facts.why: needed because the outline's kennelling beat requires the hounds' usual role and the number of dogs shut in.

facts.fact: Bhaskaran passed a salt-and-cloth cart from the coast through his gate at the last new moon on the strength of a council-wax tally, and the tally number matches the one found in the dead raider's satchel.
facts.why: needed because the outline requires a furious sergeant for Devan to calm in the hall.

facts.fact: Genuine council wax is dull brick red, pressed with a pepper-sprig mark, and poured with clove oil so it does not crack in damp. The forged tally's wax is about a month old.
facts.why: needed because the clue (C02) about genuine council wax needs a retrievable physical detail; the clove scent is the incidental detail meant to be remembered.

facts.fact: Devan tells Neela the pass-seller is someone on the queen's council and that he does not know who; he says the raiders' next targets are the coast-side villages.
facts.why: needed because the outline has Neela learn his goal in this chapter.

facts.fact: Neela finds a gap of about thirty counts under the far wall when the lower wall pair swings inward, and one sentry paces the walk above the warden's window.
facts.why: needed because she tests the night defences in the open yard, and chapter 5 has Devan pull the west-wall sentry.
